newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan kerosene demand seen picking up.
newsitem.headline: Japan kerosene demand seen picking up.

text.p: Japan's kerosene demand has started to pick up due to the onset of cold weather and will grow further as oil dealers secure domestic cargoes ahead of wholesale price increases for December, traders said on Friday.
"Kerosene demand in the (domestic) spot market will peak towards the end of the month, one step ahead of the price hikes," one middle distillate trader said.

Amid high global crude oil prices and the yen's depreciation against the dollar, major oil firms in Japan have decided to raise their wholesale kerosene prices by about four percent to 37.7-37.9 yen per litre for December.
The planned price rise has prompted oil products dealers to buy more in November than they originally planned to cover December demand with cheaper November cargoes, traders said.

"It's already very difficult to find available cargoes in the (domestic) spot market partly because of the growing appetite for kerosene and partly because of the fact that sellers are holding back," one middle distillates trader said.
Kerosene is mainly used for household heating in Japan, and domestic sales in the four-month period from November to February account for about 60 percent of the total annual sales volume.
